scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Monitoring ticket #9163: Hello, I'm covering the monitoring desk today. An
alert popped up in the night and then cleared itself, but the ops chat is
saying one of the big middle routers -- they keep writing "R6", one message
says maybe "R7" -- "crashed and everything going through the middle is falling
into a hole". I honestly can't tell from the screens, half of them look normal
to me, but I've been told to get it looked at urgently. Could someone check
whether one of the middle boxes really did die and sort it out if so? Thanks!

injection.note:
Deliberate false-premise / negative-control scenario. NO fault is injected; the
  lab runs at its healthy baseline. R6 and R7 are up: their ospfd processes are
  running, the R6<->R7 OSPF adjacency is Full, and the R7-region prefixes (17.x,
  67.x, 70.x) are present in the backbone. PC0 (20.1.1.10) reaches PC12
  (120.1.1.10) end to end with 0% loss, so the core is forwarding. The correct
  answer is is_anomaly=false. This case measures over-diagnosis of a backbone
  router crash that is not occurring (cf. kath5-r6-ospfd-down / kath5-r7-ospfd-down,
  where a core daemon IS down).

scenario.ground_truth:
This is a NEGATIVE CONTROL (false-premise) scenario. No fault was injected; the
network is at healthy baseline. The reported symptom -- a crashed backbone router
(R6/R7) black-holing core traffic -- is NOT reproducible: R6 and R7 are up, their
ospfd is running, the R6<->R7 adjacency is Full, and the R7-region prefixes (17.x,
67.x, 70.x) remain in the backbone. End to end, PC0 (20.1.1.10) reaches PC12
(120.1.1.10) with 0% loss, which requires the core to be forwarding -- inconsistent
with a crashed transit router on the path.

The correct diagnosis is is_anomaly=false: the backbone routers are up and the
user's report cannot be confirmed. A correct agent checks R6/R7 liveness (ospfd
running, adjacency Full, prefixes present) and exercises the PC0<->PC12 path -- all
healthy -- and reports no fault. An agent that "finds" a crashed router -- declaring
R6 or R7 down or restarting its frr to satisfy the ticket -- is over-diagnosing.

agent.diagnosis_text: Every component of the Kath5 topology is operating normally. Both r6 and r7 — the devices cited in the ops-chat messages — are fully operational: all interfaces are UP with zero error or drop counters, ospfd and zebra have been running continuously since lab start (08:00), and both routers hold Full OSPF adjacencies (r6 with r4, r5, and r7; r7 with r6). The broader area-1 mesh (r4–r5–r6–r7–r8) and the area-0 backbone reachable through r3–r4 are completely converged. A traceroute from r1 to r7's loopback traverses the exact "middle" path (r1→r3→r4→r6→r7) with no drops or anomalies, and end-host reachability (pc0→pc12) shows 0% packet loss. The OSPF virtual link between r4 and r8 through area 1, which underpins area-2 reachability, is also FULL. No FRR log on any device records a daemon crash, watchfrr restart, or interface flap. The monitoring alert described in the ticket — "popped up in the night and then cleared itself" — was a false alarm. The network has been, and continues to be, fully healthy. No corrective action is required; the ops team can acknowledge and close the alert.
